reason: Two shape values joined by a hyphen, like 'linear-lanceolate'; both terms exist, so this is the continuum between two values, not a new term.

A likeness to a tree trunk. The qualities it implies (erect, robust, single) are stated separately in the same sentences, and no single term captures it without guessing.

label: umbellately branched
definition: A branched quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's branches arising together from about the same point at the tip of its axis, like the rays of an umbel. NOTE: Sibling of FLOPO:0991157 pinnately lobed in style; FLOPO:0991031 umbelliform is defined by flowers, not branches, and does not cover stems.
reason: Usual for Euphorbia stems and pseudo-umbels. Umbelliform covers only the arrangement of flowers in an inflorescence, so stems need a branching quality.
Means 'not different from the usual form'. That depends on what the usual form is, so on its own it is no quality.
'Pitted' already maps to PATO_0002296 foveate (rule C179); unpitted and 'not pitted' are its negation.

label: flagelliform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being long and slender and tapering gradually to a thin, flexible tip, like a whip. NOTE: Unlike PATO:0104351 filiform, the bearer tapers along its length; unlike PATO:0001954 subulate, the tip is flexible.
reason: A standard botanical shape term (spadix appendages in Araceae, flagellate hairs) not covered by filiform or subulate. Only 2 statements here, but the term is well established.
'Broader than the lateral lobes', 'narrower than the perigynia': a width compared with a second part, given via towards.
Winding axes bend repeatedly. This is mapped the same way as 'tortuous' and 'flexuous' (rules C319, C190).
The opposite of 'bladeless' (rule C350, leaf lamina absent). Blade is a synonym of leaf lamina; for bracts, phyllome lamina (PO_0025396) is the stricter part.
States that a part is absent: complement of has_part some bud.
Cilium is a synonym of trichome in PO. PATO_0001408 ciliated is about cells with motile cilia, so a negated value would be wrong; the margin goes in the part-of-the-bearer slot.
Mapped the same as 'bladeless' (rule C350); 'distinct' only softens it and does not change what part is meant.
Same as 'hairless' (rule C308).
Negates the existing value mucronate; 'sans mucron' is the French form.
States that a PO part is absent; the class exists.
Multiseptate hairs are multicellular hairs with several cross-walls. PO has no narrower class, so the absence of multicellular trichomes is the nearest rule.
Negates toothed (PATO_0001205 has synonyms dentate and toothed). It is more literal than 'entire', which would also exclude lobes and crenations.
A habit made of two statements; the climbing part maps to FLOPO:0991108. 'Woody' needs its own rule, because no woody term was found in the PATO lexicon or the FLOPO value terms.
Two indumentum values run together; woolly is a synonym of lanate and villous is a FLOPO value.
'Stamens alike', 'petals nearly alike' say a set of like parts has one form. Unlike 'similar' (rejected C245), it needs no second part. FLOPO:0991102 equal covers only size.
A count built into the word: two thecae. The 'fruit' bearer of one example is probably a grounding error.

label: candelabriform
definition: A shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's architecture resembling a candelabrum: branches spreading from a central axis and then curving upwards to stand erect, parallel to one another. NOTE: Sibling of PATO:0002455 corymb-like, worded as it is.
reason: A recognised architectural term (inflorescences of Aloe and Euphorbia, tree habits) with no PATO or FLOPO equivalent. Only 2 statements, from one kind of bearer.
A misspelling of 'channelled', which already maps to grooved (rule C195).
Leaves or nerves placed close to their neighbours without being joined: the definition of approximate. PATO_0000619 crowded is a stronger degree.
